title: Replace Primitive with Object

solutions.title: One ShelfCode, one parser
solutions.tradeoff: Two of the three callers now answer edge-shaped shelf codes differently than they used to - a three-letter section, a book still in processing with no shelf letter yet - because there is now exactly one place that decides what a shelf code means, and that decision was never actually reviewed before. Making those two callers agree with the third was deliberately left out of this diff.

reviewFocus: Feed "FIC-813" (no shelf letter yet) through cartSection, spineLabelSection, and sectionTally as they stood in src/. Do they still disagree the way WALKTHROUGH.md's trace says, or did something already change?
Does ShelfCode.parse throw on a string that was never a valid shelf code, and is that itself a behaviour change worth its own line in a commit message - not this one?
Is ShelfCode.section used by all three callers, or did one of them keep a .slice() or a regex of its own?
Would you have widened the public signatures from string to ShelfCode, or is stopping at the string boundary the right amount of refactoring for this diff?
Is fixing cartSection's and sectionTally's edge-case answers proposed as a separate, later change - and does the walkthrough say why, not just that it should be?
